message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3.56","text":"To those who thought that he was not good (as the Scriptures say), he said, “Which of you will, if a son asks him for bread, give him a stone instead? Or if the son also asks for a fish, will he give him a snake instead? Therefore, if you, though evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give good things to those who ask him and to those who do his will?” To those who asserted that he was in a temple, he said, “Do not swear by heaven, because it is God’s throne, nor by the earth, because it is the footstool of his feet.” To those who had assumed beforehand that God desires sacrifices, he said, “God wants mercy and not sacrifices, knowledge of him and not whole burnt offerings.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τίνα ὑμῶν αἰτήσει υἱὸς ἄρτον, μὴ λίθον ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;","chosen":"Which of you will, if a son asks him for bread, give him a stone instead?","rationale":"The son is the subject of αἰτήσει, while the person addressed by τίνα ὑμῶν is the understood subject of ἐπιδώσει. The conditional English expresses the paratactic relationship, and the rhetorical question preserves μή’s expectation of a negative answer."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς αἰτουμένοις αὐτὸν","chosen":"those who ask him","rationale":"The middle-form participle is rendered idiomatically as requesting something from him."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς δὲ αὐτὸν διαβεβαιουμένοις ἐν ναῷ εἶναι","chosen":"To those who asserted that he was in a temple","rationale":"διαβεβαιόομαι conveys confident assertion; the pronoun’s referent remains as implicit as it is in the Greek."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς δὲ προλαβοῦσιν ὅτι θυσιῶν ὀρέγεται ὁ θεός","chosen":"To those who had assumed beforehand that God desires sacrifices","rationale":"Here προλαμβάνω presents a prior assumption or preconception. Unlike the preceding διαβεβαιουμένοις, it does not by itself establish that they voiced a confident assertion."},{"source_quote":"ἐπίγνωσιν αὐτοῦ","chosen":"knowledge of him","rationale":"The genitive is taken objectively, referring to knowledge of God; “recognition of him” remains a viable lexical alternative."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"μήτε τὴν γῆν, ὅτι ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ ἐστίν. τοῖς δὲ προλαβοῦσιν","issue":"The supplied edition does not print a closing quotation mark after ἐστίν before the narrative resumes with τοῖς δὲ. The syntactic boundary is clear, so the English supplies the closing quotation mark without proposing missing words.","proposed_reading":"μήτε τὴν γῆν, ὅτι ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ ἐστίν.“ τοῖς δὲ προλαβοῦσιν","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἔφη „ὁ θεὸς ἔλεος θέλει καὶ οὐ θυσίας, ἐπίγνωσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐχ ὁλοκαυτώματα.","issue":"The supplied edition opens this final quotation but prints no closing quotation mark after ὁλοκαυτώματα. The English supplies closure at the end of the intelligible quotation; this is an editorial-punctuation feature, not a restoration of wording.","proposed_reading":"ἔφη „ὁ θεὸς ἔλεος θέλει καὶ οὐ θυσίας, ἐπίγνωσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐχ ὁλοκαυτώματα.“","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.57","text":"To those who had been persuaded that he was evil (as the Scriptures say), he said, “Do not call me good, for the one who is good is one.” And again, “Become good and compassionate like the Father who is in the heavens, who makes the sun rise upon the good and the evil and brings rain upon the righteous and the unrighteous.” To those who had been deceived into supposing that there are many gods (as the Scriptures say), he said, “Hear, Israel: the Lord your God, the Lord, is one.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"μή με λέγε ἀγαθόν· ὁ γὰρ ἀγαθὸς εἷς ἐστίν","chosen":"Do not call me good, for the one who is good is one","rationale":"The masculine singular substantive ὁ ἀγαθός and masculine εἷς refer to a personal singular, “the one who is good.” The rendering preserves the unusual numerical predication without adding “God” or substituting a familiar canonical formula."},{"source_quote":"γίνεσθε ἀγαθοὶ καὶ οἰκτίρμονες","chosen":"Become good and compassionate","rationale":"γίνεσθε denotes becoming, while οἰκτίρμονες emphasizes compassion or mercy."},{"source_quote":"ὁ πατὴρ ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς","chosen":"the Father who is in the heavens","rationale":"The attributive article and phrase are represented explicitly, and the plural οὐρανοῖς is retained as “heavens.”"},{"source_quote":"φέρει τὸν ὑετὸν","chosen":"brings rain","rationale":"This preserves the verb φέρει rather than assimilating it to the wording of a familiar parallel."},{"source_quote":"πολλοὺς θεοὺς ὑπονοεῖν","chosen":"supposing that there are many gods","rationale":"ὑπονοέω denotes supposing or imagining; English supplies “there are” to express the predicate construction naturally."},{"source_quote":"κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὑμῶν κύριος εἷς ἐστίν","chosen":"the Lord your God, the Lord, is one","rationale":"The rendering retains both occurrences of κύριος and the plural possessive ὑμῶν. An alternative syntactic presentation is “The Lord, your God, is one Lord,” but the main wording more visibly preserves the repeated title and final numerical predicate."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.58","text":"All the same, Simon, recognizing that Peter was compelling him to use the Scriptures as Jesus had taught, did not want an examination of the discourse about God to take place, although Peter had changed the examination, as Simon himself had demanded, so that it would proceed by question and answer. Nevertheless, the inquiry continued for three days. As the fourth day began to dawn, Simon set out by night for Tyre in Phoenicia. Not many days later, some of those who had gone ahead came and told Peter, “Simon, performing great wonders in Tyre, has astounded many of the people there and, through many slanders, has caused you to be hated.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Πέτρος αὐτὸν συνάγει ταῖς γραφαῖς χρῆσθαι","chosen":"Peter was compelling him to use the Scriptures","rationale":"συνάγει can express constraint or compulsion in this construction; “bringing him to use” is a possible but weaker alternative."},{"source_quote":"εἰς τὸν περὶ θεοῦ λόγον ἐξέτασιν γενέσθαι","chosen":"an examination of the discourse about God to take place","rationale":"λόγος may mean discourse, teaching, or argument; “discourse” preserves the broad sense without identifying it with a particular doctrine."},{"source_quote":"μεταθεμένου τοῦ Πέτρου","chosen":"although Peter had changed the examination","rationale":"The implicit object of μετατίθημι is supplied from ἐξέτασιν, and the following phrase identifies the new question-and-answer format."},{"source_quote":"ἡ ζήτησις τριῶν ἐπεκράτησεν ἡμερῶν","chosen":"the inquiry continued for three days","rationale":"ἐπικρατέω literally suggests holding sway, but with the duration expressed by τριῶν ... ἡμερῶν it indicates that the inquiry persisted throughout that period."},{"source_quote":"τινες τῶν προόδων","chosen":"some of those who had gone ahead","rationale":"The substantival expression denotes people preceding the main party; “members of the advance party” and “forerunners” are viable alternatives."},{"source_quote":"σὲ πολλαῖς διαβολαῖς μισεῖσθαι ἐποίησεν","chosen":"through many slanders, has caused you to be hated","rationale":"The dative πολλαῖς διαβολαῖς expresses the means by which Simon caused hostility toward Peter."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὁμῶς ὁ Σίμων","issue":"The image-checked edition prints ὁμῶς, which can mean “similarly” or “in the same way.” The context permits the adversative force normally written ὅμως, “nevertheless.” “All the same” is a provisional contextual rendering, while the printed form remains unchanged and its interpretation is not certain.","proposed_reading":"ὅμως ὁ Σίμων","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.59","text":"When Peter heard this, on the following night he had the crowd of hearers assemble. All the same, when they had assembled, he said, “Since, as I was setting out toward the nations that declare that there are many gods, to proclaim and teach that God is one, ‘who created heaven and earth’ and everything in them, so that by loving him they might be able to be saved, evil got there first and, by the law of pairing, sent Simon ahead, so that, if people cease declaring that there are many gods, they may condemn those called gods on earth but suppose that there are many gods in heaven, so that, having never honored the good of sole rule, they may perish completely after punishment. And what is most terrible, because the true word possesses incomparable strength, by getting there first with his slanders he persuades them not to accept it from me at all, lest the slanderer himself be exposed as a devil in reality and the true word, once shown forth, be able to be believed. I must therefore overtake him quickly, so that the slander, if allowed to persist, does not gain complete control of everyone.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῶν ἀκροατῶν τὸν ὄχλον συνελθεῖν ἐποίησεν","chosen":"he had the crowd of hearers assemble","rationale":"The causative construction with ἐποίησεν and the infinitive indicates that Peter caused or arranged for the gathering."},{"source_quote":"τὰ ἔθνη τὰ πολλοὺς θεοὺς λέγοντα","chosen":"the nations that declare that there are many gods","rationale":"λέγειν with πολλοὺς θεούς conveys asserting the existence of many gods, not merely pronouncing the words."},{"source_quote":"τῷ τῆς συζυγίας νόμῳ","chosen":"by the law of pairing","rationale":"συζυγία denotes conjunction, yoking, or pairing and here evokes the work’s paired-agent framework; “law of conjunction” remains a viable alternative."},{"source_quote":"καταγνόντες τῶν ἐπὶ γῆς λεγομένων","chosen":"they may condemn those called gods on earth","rationale":"“Gods” is supplied from the immediately preceding πολλοὺς θεοὺς λέγειν. The more formally elliptical “those spoken of on earth” is possible but obscures the contextual referent."},{"source_quote":"τὸ τῆς μοναρχίας τιμήσαντες καλὸν","chosen":"having honored the good of sole rule","rationale":"μοναρχία denotes rule by one or sole sovereignty. The preceding μηδέποτε negates the participle: they never honor this good."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὸ μηδὲ τὴν ἀρχὴν ἀναδέξασθαί μου","chosen":"not to accept it from me at all","rationale":"αὐτό most naturally refers to the true word, while μηδὲ τὴν ἀρχήν is idiomatic for “not at all.” The more temporally explicit “not to accept it from me even at the outset” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"ὁ διαβάλλων αὐτὸς τῷ ὄντι διάβολος","chosen":"the slanderer himself be exposed as a devil in reality","rationale":"Rendering διαβάλλων as “slanderer” and διάβολος as “devil” preserves the source’s wordplay."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὸν ἐπικαταλαβεῖν","chosen":"overtake him","rationale":"ἐπικαταλαμβάνω here means catching up with someone who has gone ahead."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὁμῶς συνελθοῦσιν ἔφη","issue":"The image-checked edition again prints ὁμῶς. It can be read as “similarly,” but the context permits the adversative force “all the same,” normally written ὅμως. The main rendering is provisional, and the printed form is not treated as an OCR defect.","proposed_reading":"ὅμως συνελθοῦσιν ἔφη","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.60","text":"“Since, then, it is necessary to appoint someone in my place, one who will fill my position, let us all pray to God with one resolve, so that he himself may make evident the best of those among us, in order that, seated upon the Messiah’s chair, he may administer his church devoutly. Who, then, will be appointed? For by God’s counsel that man is shown to be blessed whom his lord will appoint over the service of his fellow servants, to give them their provisions at their proper time, neither thinking nor saying in his heart, ‘My lord is delaying his coming,’ nor beginning to beat his fellow servants while eating and drinking with both prostitutes and drunkards. And the lord of that servant will come at an hour that he does not expect and on a day that he does not know, and he will cut him in two and place the unfaithful part of him with the hypocrites.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"μιᾷ προαιρέσει","chosen":"with one resolve","rationale":"προαίρεσις denotes deliberate purpose or resolve; the phrase calls for united intention in prayer."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ὄντων ἐν ἡμῖν τὸν κρείττονα","chosen":"the best of those among us","rationale":"The comparative κρείττονα selects the superior member from the group and therefore functions contextually as “the best”; “the one who is better among us” is a more formally comparative alternative."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τῆς χριστοῦ καθέδρας","chosen":"upon the Messiah’s chair","rationale":"χριστός functions independently as a title and is rendered “Messiah”; καθέδρα denotes an authoritative seat or chair."},{"source_quote":"τὴν αὐτοῦ ἐκκλησίαν εὐσεβῶς οἰκονομῇ","chosen":"he may administer his church devoutly","rationale":"οἰκονομέω denotes managing or administering, while εὐσεβῶς describes reverent or devout conduct. The pronoun’s precise antecedent remains implicit in English as in Greek."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τῆς θεραπείας τῶν συνδούλων αὐτοῦ","chosen":"over the service of his fellow servants","rationale":"θεραπεία may denote service, attendance, care, or a body of household attendants. “Over the care of his fellow servants” and “over the household of his fellow servants” are contextual alternatives."},{"source_quote":"μὴ ἐννοούμενον καὶ λέγοντα ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ Χρονίζει ὁ κύριός μου ἐλθεῖν καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς συνδούλους αὐτοῦ","chosen":"neither thinking nor saying in his heart, ‘My lord is delaying his coming,’ nor beginning to beat his fellow servants","rationale":"The main rendering takes μή broadly over the coordinated misconduct, keeping it within the characterization or warning attached to the appointed man. English “neither ... nor” expresses that broad negative scope. A narrower reading—“not taking thought, and saying ... and beginning”—is grammatically possible and more directly anticipates the ensuing punishment, but it turns the latter actions into affirmative narrative and fits the description of the blessed appointee less readily."},{"source_quote":"Χρονίζει ὁ κύριός μου ἐλθεῖν","chosen":"My lord is delaying his coming","rationale":"χρονίζειν with an infinitive means taking a long time or delaying the action. Lowercase “lord” preserves the servant-master imagery without deciding whether a divine referent is foregrounded."},{"source_quote":"διχοτομήσει αὐτόν","chosen":"he will cut him in two","rationale":"This preserves the literal and violent image of διχοτομέω rather than weakening it to “punish severely.”"},{"source_quote":"τὸ ἀπιστοῦν αὐτοῦ μέρος μετὰ τῶν ὑποκριτῶν θήσει","chosen":"place the unfaithful part of him with the hypocrites","rationale":"The neuter participle ἀπιστοῦν directly qualifies μέρος, producing the unusual image of an unfaithful or unbelieving part of the servant. The rendering does not replace it with the textually different idea of assigning the servant a portion."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"μὴ ἐννοούμενον καὶ λέγοντα ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ Χρονίζει ὁ κύριός μου ἐλθεῖν καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς συνδούλους αὐτοῦ, ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων μετά τε πορνῶν καὶ μεθυόντων","issue":"The construction begins with accusative participles connected to ὃν, shifts to the finite subjunctive ἄρξηται, and then uses the nominative participles ἐσθίων and πίνων. The scope of μή is also uncertain. The main text takes it broadly over the coordinated misconduct because the surrounding clause identifies the appointed man as blessed and charges him with timely provision. A narrower scope, in which only ἐννοούμενον is negated and the saying and abuse are affirmative, remains possible and better prepares for the following punishment. The sentence is anacoluthic, but both readings arise from the supplied wording and no conjectural restoration is required.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
